title: Lock, Stock and Two Smoking Barrels
logline: Four London friends stake £100,000 on a rigged card game, lose it plus another £500,000, and have one week to find the money.
note: His film debut. He plays a street hustler, which he had actually been.

title: Snatch
logline: A stolen 84-carat diamond works its way through London's underworld while a small-time boxing promoter tries to survive a fixed fight gone wrong.
note: He narrates. Brad Pitt plays a bare-knuckle boxer nobody can understand.

title: The Transporter
logline: A getaway driver who lives by three rules breaks all of them when the package in his trunk turns out to be a woman.
note: Rule one: never change the deal. Rule two: no names. Rule three: never open the package. There is also an oil fight.

title: Transporter 2
logline: Now chauffeuring a Miami official's young son, Frank has to get the boy back after a kidnapping tied to a lethal virus.
note: The Audi does a barrel roll to scrape a bomb off its undercarriage. Physics has filed a complaint.

title: Chaos
logline: A suspended Seattle detective is reinstated to negotiate a bank hostage standoff, then chases a heist that isn't what it looks like.
note: Wesley Snipes, a rookie Ryan Phillippe, and a surprising amount of chaos theory.

title: Revolver
logline: A gambler fresh out of prison goes after the casino boss who put him there, with help from two loan sharks playing a longer game.
note: Guy Ritchie read several books about chess and the ego and put all of them in this one.

title: Crank
logline: A hitman injected with a synthetic poison has to keep his adrenaline up or his heart stops.
note: The premise is the plot is the premise.

title: War
logline: An FBI agent spends years hunting the assassin who killed his partner while a yakuza–triad war erupts around them.
note: Statham versus Jet Li, with a third-act twist that rewrites everything before it.

title: The Bank Job
logline: A London car dealer with debts is recruited to tunnel into a Baker Street bank vault in 1971, where the deposit boxes hold more than cash.
note: Loosely based on a real 1971 robbery. The closest he has come to a period drama.

title: In the Name of the King
logline: A farmer named Farmer takes on a sorcerer's army after it kills his son and carries off his wife.
note: A Uwe Boll fantasy epic adapted from the video game Dungeon Siege. Burt Reynolds plays the king. Ray Liotta plays a wizard.

title: Death Race
logline: A framed ex-racer is forced to compete in a prison's televised armored car race behind the mask of its dead champion, Frankenstein.
note: Joan Allen, a three-time Oscar nominee, delivers the most quotable line in the film. It cannot be printed here.

title: Transporter 3
logline: Frank is fitted with a bracelet that detonates if he strays from his car, and saddled with a passenger he never agreed to.
note: The bracelet rule is the best rule the franchise ever made.

title: Crank: High Voltage
logline: Chev survives the fall and wakes up with his heart stolen, replaced by an artificial one that needs constant electrical charge.
note: Somehow more Crank than Crank.

title: The Expendables
logline: A crew of ageing mercenaries takes a job to topple a dictator on a Gulf island and finds a rogue ex-CIA man running the show.
note: The one ensemble film on the calendar, admitted on a technicality: his character's name is Lee Christmas.

title: The Mechanic
logline: A meticulous hitman takes on an apprentice: the son of the mentor he was ordered to kill.
note: A remake of the 1972 Charles Bronson film. Ben Foster plays the apprentice with maximum Ben Foster.

title: Blitz
logline: A short-fused London detective hunts a serial killer who is murdering police officers.
note: Paddy Considine co-stars. The opening scene involves car thieves and a hurling stick, and sets the tone.

title: Killer Elite
logline: A retired mercenary is forced back to work to save his mentor, hunting ex-SAS men guarded by a secret society of former soldiers.
note: Robert De Niro plays the mentor. Clive Owen wears a moustache like it is a job.

title: Safe
logline: A disgraced cage fighter becomes the protector of a young math prodigy carrying a code the Russian mob, the triads and dirty cops all want.
note: He crosses most of Manhattan on foot, and the city pays for it.

title: Parker
logline: A professional thief left for dead by his crew follows them to Palm Beach to take back his share.
note: Adapted from Donald E. Westlake's Parker novels. Jennifer Lopez co-stars.

title: Hummingbird
logline: A homeless ex-special forces soldier squats in an empty London flat, takes a new name, and goes after the people who hurt his friend.
note: Released in the US as Redemption. Written and directed by the creator of Peaky Blinders.

title: Homefront
logline: A widowed ex-DEA agent moves to small-town Louisiana with his daughter and runs into a meth cook with a grudge.
note: Screenplay by Sylvester Stallone. James Franco plays the meth cook, whose name is Gator.

title: Wild Card
logline: A Las Vegas bodyguard with a gambling problem takes on a mobster's son while trying to win enough to leave town for good.
note: Written by William Goldman, who also wrote The Princess Bride.

title: Mechanic: Resurrection
logline: Arthur Bishop is dragged out of retirement and forced to stage three impossible "accidents" to save a kidnapped woman.
note: Jessica Alba, Tommy Lee Jones and Michelle Yeoh all signed up for this.

title: The Meg
logline: A rescue diver is called back to face a prehistoric megalodon that escapes from the depths of the Mariana Trench.
note: The highest-grossing film on this calendar. The shark deserves co-billing.

title: Wrath of Man
logline: A quiet new guard at a Los Angeles armored-truck company turns out to be very good at the job and very interested in who robbed it.
note: A remake of the French thriller Le Convoyeur. The coldest film on the calendar.

title: Operation Fortune: Ruse de Guerre
logline: An MI6 contractor recruits a movie star to get close to a billionaire arms dealer before a stolen device called the Handle is sold.
note: Hugh Grant plays the arms dealer and is having the time of his life.

title: Meg 2: The Trench
logline: A deep dive into the Trench turns up more megs, an illegal mining operation, and worse.
note: Directed by Ben Wheatley of Kill List, which gets funnier the longer you think about it.

title: The Beekeeper
logline: A retired operative from a secret program called the Beekeepers dismantles the phishing ring that scammed his kind neighbor.
note: The bee metaphors do not let up for one second.

title: A Working Man
logline: An ex-Royal Marine working construction in Chicago goes looking for his boss's kidnapped daughter and finds a trafficking ring.
note: Co-written by Sylvester Stallone. Shot under the title Levon's Trade.

title: Shelter
logline: A former MI6 assassin living alone on a Hebridean island rescues a teenage girl from a storm, and the rescue puts him back on his old employer's radar.
note: Set largely on a remote Scottish island. The weather gets second billing.

title: Mutiny
logline: A bodyguard framed for his employer's murder boards a cargo ship under a dead assassin's identity to find the people who set him up.
note: Amazon accidentally put it on Prime Video two days before it opened in cinemas.
